sourceCopy.name: Heart Rate Zone Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Heart Rate Zone Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Free heart rate zones by age or Karvonen. Set a measured maximum and custom cutoffs; see bpm ranges.
sourceCopy.intro: Estimate five exercise heart-rate zones from an age-based maximum or a maximum you already know. Choose percentage-of-maximum or Karvonen reserve, then adjust each zone boundary.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do I calculate heart rate zones?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Choose a method and six increasing percentage boundaries. Percentage-of-maximum multiplies your maximum heart rate by each cutoff. Karvonen adds that percentage of heart-rate reserve (maximum minus resting heart rate) to your resting rate. The age estimate uses 220 minus age; it is only a rough population estimate.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The calculation runs in this browser. Your age, heart rates and zone cutoffs are not uploaded or saved by this tool.
howTo: Choose percentage of maximum or Karvonen heart-rate reserve.
Use the rough 220-minus-age estimate or enter a maximum heart rate you already know; Karvonen also needs resting heart rate.
Edit the six increasing percentages that define five adjacent zones, then calculate and review the bpm ranges.

fields.boundaryNote: Set six strictly increasing cutoffs from 0 to 100%. They create five adjacent zones; start with the defaults or customize them.
fields.tableCaption: Estimated zone cutoffs (lower edge included; upper edge is the next boundary)
fields.accuracyNote: A common estimate is maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age, but it is not a measurement and can differ substantially for an individual. The default 50–100% cutoffs are only an editable partition, not a recommendation or the AHA target range; AHA describes a general target of about 50–85% of estimated maximum for moderate-to-vigorous activity.
fields.safetyNote: Medicines and health conditions can change heart-rate response. If you have a heart condition, take medicine that affects heart rate, are pregnant, are under 18, or need a personal exercise target, ask a qualified health professional. Stop activity and seek appropriate help for concerning symptoms. The CDC talk test is another way to judge relative effort.

fields.privacyNote: All inputs stay in this browser; nothing is uploaded or stored.

messages.ageRange: Enter an adult age from 18 to 100 years.
messages.maximumRange: Enter a known maximum heart rate from 80 to 240 bpm.
messages.restingRange: Enter a resting heart rate from 30 to 120 bpm.
messages.maxMustExceedRest: Maximum heart rate must be higher than resting heart rate.
messages.boundaryRange: Zone percentages must be whole numbers from 0 to 100.
messages.boundaryOrder: Zone boundaries must increase from left to right.

additionalFaqs.question: What is the Karvonen formula?
additionalFaqs.answer: It estimates a target rate as resting heart rate plus a chosen fraction of heart-rate reserve. Reserve is maximum heart rate minus resting heart rate. This result is still an estimate, not an individualized prescription.

additionalFaqs.question: Is 220 minus age an exact maximum heart rate?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. It is a rough age-based population estimate cited by the American Heart Association, not a measurement of your own maximum. Fitness, health, medication and individual variation can affect heart rate.

additionalFaqs.question: Are heart-rate zones medical limits?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. These ranges are configurable arithmetic estimates for general education. A clinician can help set personal targets, especially with a heart condition or medicine that affects heart rate.
